name: Future forms: will, going to, present continuous
subtitle: English has three main ways to talk about the future. Use will for quick decisions, promises and opinions: I'll help you. Use going to for plans and things you can see coming: I'm going to study law. Use the present continuous for fixed arrangements: I'm meeting Sam at six.
source: icanspeak English original English text (grammar-b1 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: 'It's cold in here.' 'I'll close the window.' · I'm going to learn the guitar. · We're meeting Sam at six.

qa.html: will + base verb. The form is the same for every person: I'll, you'll, she'll, we'll, they'll. Negative: won't. Question: Will you …? I'll call you. She won't come. Will it rain?

Use will when you decide now, when you promise or offer something, and when you give an opinion about the future (often with I think, probably, perhaps): 'I'm thirsty.' 'I'll get you some water.' I'll be on time, I promise. I think Mia will pass.

am / is / are + going to + base verb. Use it for a plan you made before you speak: I'm going to learn Spanish. We're going to buy a flat. Also use it when you can see that something is about to happen: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain!

Use the present continuous for an arrangement: you have fixed a time and a place, often with another person. I'm seeing the dentist at ten. We're flying to Rome on Saturday. There is usually a time word.

Plan or arrangement? They often mean the same, and both are fine: We're going to visit / We're visiting my aunt on Sunday. Use going to when it is only your idea. Use the present continuous when it is fixed. Deciding now? Use will.

✗ I will to help you. → ✓ I'll help you. (no to after will) · ✗ When I will arrive, I'll call you. → ✓ When I arrive, I'll call you. (present after when) · ✗ The phone's ringing. I'm going to get it. → ✓ I'll get it. (you decide now)

concept.noteHtml: After when, if, as soon as, before and until we use the present, not will: I'll text you as soon as I get home. (see Time clauses and Conditionals). For timetables the present simple is normal: The train leaves at nine. For offers, British speakers also say Shall I …? and Shall we …?: Shall I open the window? Learn the present continuous form first in Present continuous. For other ways to talk about possibility, see Modal verbs.

rounds.label: 1 · Plans with going to
rounds.instruction: You hear a plan in the present simple. Say it with going to.

example.answer: I'm going to learn the guitar.

items.prompt: Tom starts a new job next month.
items.answer: Tom is going to start a new job next month.

items.prompt: We buy a car next year.
items.answer: We're going to buy a car next year.

items.prompt: Amira studies law at university.
items.answer: Amira is going to study law at university.

items.prompt: I paint the kitchen this weekend.
items.answer: I'm going to paint the kitchen this weekend.

items.prompt: They move to Leeds in May.
items.answer: They're going to move to Leeds in May.

items.prompt: Priya takes her driving test next week.
items.answer: Priya is going to take her driving test next week.

rounds.label: 2 · Statement → question with will
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence with will. Ask the question.

items.prompt: You'll be at home tonight.
items.answer: Will you be at home tonight?

items.prompt: They'll win the match.
He'll come to the party.
items.answer: Will he come to the party?

items.prompt: It'll rain tomorrow.
We'll need a taxi.
Kwame will bring the cake.

exercises.title: Be going to: am, is or are?
exercises.hint: Choose the form of be that fits the subject.

items.prompt: I ___ going to buy a new laptop.
items.why: I goes with am: I am going to.

items.prompt: Mei ___ going to start a course in September.
items.why: She / he / it goes with is.

items.prompt: We ___ going to visit my aunt in Leeds.
Zofia and Diego ___ going to get married next year.
Look at the sky! It ___ going to snow.
Where ___ you going to stay in London?
items.why: You goes with are, also in questions.

items.prompt: My brother ___ not going to come to the party.
items.why: He goes with is. Negative: is not / isn't going to.

exercises.title: Which form is it: will, going to or present continuous?
exercises.hint: Look at the clue: decision now, plan, arrangement or evidence.

items.prompt: 'I can't open this door.' 'I'll help you.' Form: ___
items.hint: A decision at the moment of speaking.
items.why: The speaker decides now and offers help: will.

items.prompt: 'I'm going to paint my room. I bought the paint yesterday.' Form: ___
items.why: The idea is older than the moment of speaking: going to.

items.prompt: 'I'm seeing the dentist at ten. I booked it last week.' Form: ___
items.why: The appointment is booked, with a time: present continuous.

items.prompt: 'Be careful! You're going to spill your tea.' Form: ___
items.why: The speaker sees that it is about to happen: going to.

items.prompt: 'I think Tom will win the race.' Form: ___
items.why: An opinion about the future: will.

items.prompt: 'We're flying to Rome on Saturday. We've got the tickets.' Form: ___
items.why: The trip is arranged and has a day: present continuous.

items.prompt: 'Don't worry, I promise I won't tell anyone.' Form: ___
